key_insight: Glass does storage, silicon does amplification: transferred Si sense chiplets fix TFT sense-amp offset while IGZO 2T0C tiers keep transistor-written, endurance-safe writes on depreciated display lines.
killer_doubt: Chiplets every 3 mm imply ~1.5 mm bitlines (~300 fF, 60x a 5 fF cell), so TFT preamps are needed anyway; panel steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um, not 0.3 um.
decisive_experiment: On Gen-2 glass, build one IGZO 2T0C tier at 0.5-1 um with TFT 8:1 local mux plus micro-transfer-printed 28 nm sense chiplets. Measure chiplet contact yield, sense margin versus bitline length, and 85 C retention. ~$400k.
prior_art: Phase B N-38 panel oxide memory and N-36 glass-carried tiers; R27's I-01819 R2R IGZO; SEL/Sharp CAAC-IGZO memory; X-Celeprint micro-transfer printing [training knowledge].

key_insight: Pre-latch charge gain would trade capacitor height for periphery, but the read side is already solved without gain by charge-transfer pre-sensing (N-04).
killer_doubt: EMCCD stages give only ~1-1.6% gain each at 40-50 V clocks; 1.2x per stage needs near-avalanche fields, excess noise (F~1.4) and gain spread far beyond 5 V periphery.
decisive_experiment: Not worth funding. If pursued: a 180 nm MPW with 10-gate high-field registers, measuring gain versus clock voltage and spread across 1,000 registers. Pass: 5x total at <=5 V with sigma <10%. ~$100k.
prior_art: EMCCD gain registers (TI Impactron, e2v L3Vision); Z-RAM impact ionisation; Mitsubishi charge-transfer presensing DRAM (JSSC 1997) [training knowledge]; study N-04; I-05065/I-02889 dropped.

key_insight: Decompression overlapped with tRCD hides MXT's latency; zero-run coding of sparse activations and KV caches could add ~1.3-2x effective capacity without new cells.
killer_doubt: The 10x double-counts 4:1 quantization software already applies; DRAM-process logic (3-4 metals, slow FETs) makes row-wide decoders costly, and variable-length rows need remap metadata.
decisive_experiment: Trace study: compress real INT4/FP8 weights, KV caches and activations at row granularity (2-8 KB) with zero-run and table codes; report gain beyond quantization net of metadata. Proceed only if >1.5x. ~$40k.
prior_art: IBM MXT (2001); LCP (MICRO 2013); Buddy Compression (ISCA 2020); Marvell Structera A inline LZ4; ZeroPoint compression IP; study N-69.

key_insight: Mirrored predictors at both ends of a link send only residuals; a cheap FPGA proof, and residual coding stacks with any link PHY.
killer_doubt: General memory traffic compresses ~1.3-1.5x, I/O is only part of the 10-20 pJ/bit, every miss pays 2-5 ns of codec latency, and link compression is decades old.
decisive_experiment: Replay SPEC, graph and LLM memory traces through last-value, stride and zero-run predictors in software; measure bits saved and codec latency. Stop below 1.5x. ~$20k, not $600k.
prior_art: Memory-link compression (Thuresson et al., IEEE TC 2008); base-delta-immediate compression (PACT 2012); GPU delta colour compression; value prediction (Lipasti 1996) [training knowledge].

key_insight: A 0.2 fF local node gets a >20 sigma signal from ~3% of the cell charge, so 64 B could be read without restoring a whole 8 KB row.
killer_doubt: Subthreshold sip is exponential in Vt: at ~80 mV/dec, +/-6-sigma Vt (~+/-250 mV) spreads sipped charge >1,000x; the self-limiting fix needs an amplifier per ~3 cells.
decisive_experiment: SPICE Monte Carlo with foundry Vt statistics, then a 28 nm MPW of 0.2 fF local nodes on short bitlines: measure sipped-charge spread over 1e5 cells and cell droop after 16 reads. ~$120k.
prior_art: Fine-grained activation (Udipi, ISCA 2010; FGDRAM, MICRO 2017); non-destructive 2T0C gain cells (imec, Kioxia); study N-04 [training knowledge].

key_insight: Periphery-under-cell bonding is coming anyway; an open cut at the ~1 um-pitch local-bitline level lets array-only fabs and U.S. logic foundries each make half the die.
killer_doubt: Bond pitch of 0.4-1 um against ~0.05-0.08 um bitline pairs keeps an 8-32:1 mux on the array wafer (Cbl ~10-12 fF); incumbents have no reason to sell array wafers.
decisive_experiment: Draft the cut at 64-cell bitlines with 8:1 mux (N-40); tape out a 28 nm periphery MPW die; wafer-bond at ~1 um to a third-party IGZO or MIM array wafer. Measure per-bond yield over 1e6 bonds and sense margin. ~$500k.
prior_art: YMTC Xtacking, Kioxia CBA (NAND, in-house); UniIC SeDRAM; YMTC bonded-DRAM patents and no open standard (via search snippet); Samsung/SK hynix 4F2 periphery-under-cell.

key_insight: Silicon-proven open sense-amp, pump and hammer-tracker blocks only matter once periphery moves to a logic wafer; then they cut an entrant's design cost.
killer_doubt: Entry barriers are cell process, yield learning and capex, not circuit IP: a ~$50-100M design saving against a $15B+ fab. DRAM-side periphery lives in the DRAM process.
decisive_experiment: Fold into I-04714: open-source that tape-out's 28 nm periphery die (offset-calibrated sense amps, decoders, hammer tracker) and measure reuse by two outside teams. Adds ~$100k.
prior_art: OpenRAM (UCSC); LiteDRAM and DRAM Bender (controller side); commercial DDR5/LPDDR5 PHYs (Synopsys, Cadence, Rambus); similar I-04102 dropped.

key_insight: An open gain-cell macro compiler on SKY130/GF180 gives domestic mature fabs a block 2-3x denser than SRAM and trains memory designers.
killer_doubt: A 130 nm 3T cell is ~1-2 um2 against ~0.001 um2 for 1b DRAM, >1,000x less dense, with ms-scale retention; it does not touch DRAM supply.
decisive_experiment: Not needed for this study. If funded: one SKY130 MPW (~$10-50k) of compiler output, measuring retention distribution at 85 C and density against OpenRAM SRAM macros.
prior_art: OpenRAM on SKY130 (Guthaus, UCSC); open gain-cell compilers (OpenGCRAM, 2025) [training knowledge]; Teman/Giterman and Burg gain-cell eDRAM; similar I-01800 dropped.

key_insight: Coating the reference electrode with the same molecules makes the sense ladder track each redox plateau through temperature and ageing: a genuinely clever self-calibration.
killer_doubt: Ideal surface redox peaks are ~90 mV wide at 25 C, so seven plateaus need ~1.4 V; counter-ion motion through solid electrolyte has not shown 50 ns switching (N-17's test).
decisive_experiment: University electrochemistry: graft a 3-couple mixture on porous TiN under a solid polymer electrolyte; pulse 50 ns-1 us; measure charge per plateau, level overlap at 85 C and drift over 1e9 cycles. ~$200k.
prior_art: ZettaCore porphyrin memory, including multi-state sandwich molecules (Bocian, Lindsey, 2000s) [training knowledge]; study N-17 ZettaCore revival (ALIVE-SPECULATIVE).

key_insight: Retention profiling with a Bloom-filter weak-row list can cut refresh ~4x on commodity parts and could ship as licensable controller RTL.
killer_doubt: DDR5 on-die ECC hides raw retention failures and VRT cells drift, forcing guardbands; RAIDR, REAPER and HARP already map this, and DDR5 refresh is internally sequenced.
decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender on 20 DDR5 parts: profile at 256 ms and 85 C, then run 30 days of ACT-only weak-row refresh with REF thinned; count escapes from VRT and on-die ECC. ~$80k.
prior_art: RAIDR (ISCA 2012), AVATAR (DSN 2015), REAPER (ISCA 2017), HARP (MICRO 2021); DRAM Bender (2022); study N-42/N-63.

key_insight: In a 4x price spike, bin-failing dies with sparse bad bits are cheap supply; a CXL buffer with remapping and strong ECC can resell them as a far-memory grade.
killer_doubt: Most final-test rejects are gross failures (IDD, speed, whole mats), so recovery may add only ~2-5% supply; 1e-2 raw BER needs ~15-20% parity and 4 KB read-modify-write.
decisive_experiment: Buy ~500 off-bin and broker-scrap DDR4/DDR5 parts; map fail bits with DRAM Bender at 85 C; compute the fraction usable under page remap plus Chipkill, and its $/GB. ~$150k.
prior_art: Micron SpecTek downgraded parts; X-PPR (CAL 2025) recycled-DDR4 repair in CXL; ArchShield (ISCA 2013); Meta CXL DDR4 reuse.

key_insight: Differential sensing against a matched twin is the right instinct for sneak currents, as core memory cancelled half-select noise by weaving its sense wire.
killer_doubt: Sneak current depends on data in ~N half-selected cells, so a twin cancels only with identical data (half the density); resistive elements endure ~1e6-1e9 cycles versus >=3e8 needed.
decisive_experiment: SPICE a 32-plane vertical crosspoint with measured self-rectifying RRAM I-V and random data in both pillars; report read margin versus array size. Stop unless margin survives 64x64 planes. ~$30k.
prior_art: Self-rectifying selectorless vertical RRAM and reference-line sneak-current subtraction, widely studied in crosspoint literature [training knowledge]; 1950s core-memory sense-wire weaving.
